A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KDS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original mixture-of-Gaussians simulations, super-resolution and ImageNet inpainting experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds mode-seeking comparisons and experiments on KDS variants.

M1.justification: The default patch-wise steering procedure and Algorithms 1–5 remain unchanged. v2 adds optional procedural variants: CLIPIQA-based final selection after KDS in Appendix A.1.7, and Laplacian-kernel and automatic-bandwidth variants in Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic mixture task, super-resolution on DIV2K, RealSR, DRealSR and degraded DF2K, and ImageNet box inpainting. Deblurring, medical imaging and video restoration are proposed future applications, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands direct comparisons by evaluating High Density Sampling (HDS) and Density-Guided Sampling (DGS) against KDS on RealSR with DiffBIR (Tables 5 and 11). It also introduces an L2-guidance comparator in Table 12. InDI receives conceptual discussion but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, backbones, sampling settings and metrics are retained. Additional experiments introduce HDS/DGS parameter sweeps, alternative kernels and bandwidth selection, post-KDS CLIPIQA selection, and a patch-size-4 configuration with 40 particles. These extend settings within existing tasks rather than revise the original evaluations.

E4.justification: Appendices A.1.7 and A.2 add substantial analyses of whether KDS helps subsequent Best-of-N selection, sensitivity of HDS/DGS, kernel guidance versus L2 guidance, automatic bandwidth selection, and joint patch-size/particle-count changes. The earlier robustness, bandwidth, patch-size and CFG analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without statistical testing annotations. v2 adds P < 0.05 significance markers to Tables 1–2 and reports ±σ and significance in Table 5. The test, source of σ and repeated-run counts are unspecified, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but Tables 5 and 10–14 add substantial comparison and variant results. For example, Table 5 reports HDS at 24.56 PSNR/0.386 LPIPS versus KDS at 24.39/0.339; Table 14 adds 22.70/0.281 for patch size 4 with 40 particles. These are new comparison/configuration results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The introduction replaces noisy-latent KDE and additive guidance equations with clean-prediction consensus, explicit score definitions and a weighted-score ODE. The later patch-wise mathematics and algorithms remain unchanged, and no proofs are added. The new Eq. (2) has a score-sign inconsistency with the relation retained in Section 2.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free, patch-wise ensemble steering improves fidelity, perception and robustness in super-resolution and inpainting. Additional experiments support this existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations distinguishing KDS from HDS, DGS and InDI, and argues that KDS makes subsequent Best-of-N selection more reliable. It also interprets automatic bandwidth selection as removing tedious tuning, replacing v1's explicit tuning limitation, and claims larger particle ensembles enable effective larger patches. Computational overhead remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 documents HDS/DGS sweep values, identifies the median bandwidth heuristic and manual h=0.3 comparison, and adds runtime/memory reporting to the appendix BoN table, including 28.9 seconds and 10.4 Gb for CLIPIQA selection. Existing pseudocode, training details and checkpoint-access instructions are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 5 substantially expands positioning against closely related mode-seeking approaches HDS and DGS and distinguishes KDS from the already cited InDI. Their two references and a denoising overview are added. Publication metadata updates for existing references do not constitute additional related works.

P1.justification: The introductory explanation is locally rewritten, Discussion and separate Limitations & Future Work sections are added, and new appendix analyses shift subsequent subsection numbering. Terminology and typographical corrections accompany these changes, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially through a main-text mode-seeking comparison and appendix tables covering selection and component analyses. Existing tables gain statistical annotations or resource columns. Figures 1–15 retain their content; Figure 8 is repositioned to accommodate the new analysis.

improvement.justification: Direct HDS/DGS comparisons and the new component analyses provide useful evidence missing from v1 about KDS's comparative performance and practical robustness. The gain is limited by unexplained statistical testing and σ estimation, a new score-sign inconsistency in the introduction, and Table 14 changing patch size and particle count together. The unchanged algorithms and original results preserve the paper's empirical foundation.
